boot-order-drive-probe.desc: four SATA drives were added in one pass (2 HDD + 2 SSD) during the 2026-08-27 reassembly.
boot-order-drive-probe.gate: operator pastes target output back; agent records it with: node tools/cmd.ts result boot-order-drive-probe
boot-order-drive-probe.rollback: exact inverse required before any forward re-run (MASTER qualityGate)
boot-order-drive-probe.instructions:
id -u
# boot-order-drive-probe.block - ROOT shell on the target (sudo -i first, then paste). READ-ONLY.
# Why: four SATA drives were added in one pass (2 HDD + 2 SSD) during the 2026-08-27 reassembly.
# Firmware can inject new SATA boot entries and push them ahead of the NVMe ZBM entry, causing
# the primary display (NVIDIA/3080) to stay dark while the BIOS probes SATA - the tertiary
# monitor sees POST video earlier because it gets the framebuffer during firmware init.
# This block: (1) reads the true EFI BootOrder and every boot variable, (2) identifies all drives
# by stable /dev/disk/by-id names, (3) reads lsblk with partition types and UUIDs, (4) reads the
# ZBM and pool health, and (5) reads dmesg for any boot-device scan timing or SATA errors.
# Nothing is changed. Paste the FULL output back.
efibootmgr -v
cat /proc/cmdline
uname -r
findmnt /
df -h /
lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE,FSTYPE,LABEL,PARTTYPE,UUID,MODEL,SERIAL
ls -l /dev/disk/by-id
ls -l /dev/disk/by-path
zpool status
zpool list -v
zfs list -o name,mountpoint,used,avail
dmesg -T | grep -i -E 'ata|sata|sda|sdb|sdc|sdd|nvme|boot|efi|timeout|error' | head -80
dmesg -T | grep -i 'ahci\|rst\|nvme\|blk_update' | head -40

boot-order-nvme-first.gate: operator pastes target output back; agent records it with: node tools/cmd.ts result boot-order-nvme-first
boot-order-nvme-first.rollback: if the machine does not boot, enter BIOS (F10) -> Boot tab -> set boot order manually
boot-order-nvme-first.instructions:
id -u
# boot-order-nvme-first.block - ROOT shell on the target (sudo -i first, then paste).
# OPERATOR-GATED: run only after boot-order-drive-probe.block output is pasted back and the
# ZBM boot entry numbers are confirmed (expected Boot0002 and Boot0008 per prior receipts).
# PURPOSE: remove any SATA/HDD boot entries the firmware auto-created when the four drives were
# added, and set BootOrder so nvme ZBM (Boot0002) is first, Boot0008 second, nothing else.
# This is the authoritative fix for the main-monitor display delay: when SATA entries sit ahead
# of the NVMe entry, firmware scans each SATA device (hundreds of ms each in RAID mode) before
# handing off to ZBM, and the 3080 gets no mode-set signal until after that scan.
# ROLLBACK: if the machine does not boot, enter BIOS (F10) -> Boot tab -> set boot order manually
# to the ZBM NVMe entry, or press F9 at HP splash to pick the NVMe device directly.
# ---
# STEP 1: show current state (confirm entry numbers before deleting anything)
efibootmgr -v
# ---
# STEP 2: read actual BootOrder bytes (cross-check)
cat /sys/firmware/efi/efivars/BootOrder-8be4df61-93ca-11d2-aa0d-00e098032b8c | xxd | head -4
# ---
# STEP 3: OPERATOR READS the output above and confirms which Boot#### numbers are SATA/HDD entries
# injected by firmware (not the ZBM entries Boot0002 and Boot0008).
# Then operator pastes this block back with the SATA entry numbers filled in below.
# Example: if firmware added Boot0003 (SATA SSD) and Boot0004 (SATA HDD), delete those two.
# DO NOT delete Boot0002 or Boot0008 (ZBM NVMe entries). DO NOT proceed without reading step 1.
# ---
# STEP 4: set BootOrder to NVMe ZBM first - run this ONLY after step 3 confirms the numbers
# Rollback value is whatever efibootmgr -v printed for BootOrder above; note it before running.
efibootmgr --bootorder 0002,0008
efibootmgr -v

oc-p10-cpu-run.desc: ParkControl is Windows-only. On Linux the same ideas live in cpupower (governor = who decides cores sleep/boost) and the intel_pstate EPP setting. Real 12700KF OC is BIOS-only (docs/oc-cpu-bios-checklist.md).
oc-p10-cpu-run.gate: read outputs first (frequency-info + idle-info + status). After set, governor prints performance and EPP prints balance_performance.
oc-p10-cpu-run.rollback: exact inverse required before any forward re-run (MASTER qualityGate)
oc-p10-cpu-run.instructions:
id -u
# oc-p10-cpu-run.block - ROOT shell. Linux-native park-control equivalent: CPU governor + EPP for bench runs, plus the meters we use on CPU power.
# Why: ParkControl is Windows-only. On Linux the same ideas live in cpupower (governor = who decides cores sleep/boost) and the intel_pstate EPP setting. Real 12700KF OC is BIOS-only (docs/oc-cpu-bios-checklist.md).
# Gate: read outputs first (frequency-info + idle-info + status). After set, governor prints performance and EPP prints balance_performance.
# Rollback at bottom: governor back to powersave and EPP back to balance_power.
# STEP 1 - read current CPU state
df -h /
cpupower frequency-info
cpupower idle-info
head -1 /sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_pstate/status
head -1 /sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_pstate/no_turbo
head -1 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_governor
head -1 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/energy_performance_preference
# STEP 2 - set bench mode (performance governor keeps cores ready; EPP balance_performance favors boost)
cpupower frequency-set -g performance
cpupower frequency-set -e balance_performance
head -1 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_governor
head -1 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/energy_performance_preference
# STEP 3 - run the CPU benchmark in another terminal, and CPU watt meter here (Ctrl+C to stop, prints a summary row of PkgWatt, Busy%, Bzy_MHz, C6):
turbostat --quiet
# STEP 4 - after bench, revert to daily settings:
cpupower frequency-set -g powersave
cpupower frequency-set -e balance_power
head -1 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_governor
head -1 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/energy_performance_preference
date

oc-p6-install.desc: operator wants official benchmarks (Geekbench 6 + Unigine Superposition) and Linux-native OC tooling (gwe, cpupower, lm_sensors, nvtop), plus power/thermal meters and CPU stability stress (stress-ng, turbostat).
oc-p6-install.gate: xbps transaction completes; command -v lines each print a path; /usr/local/bin/geekbench6 exists and ls -l shows the Geekbench dir.
oc-p6-install.rollback: xbps-remove -y gwe lm_sensors cpupower nvtop stress-ng turbostat wget then rm /usr/local/bin/geekbench6 then rm -rf /opt/geekbench then rm /root/Geekbench-6.5.0-Linux.tar.gz
oc-p6-install.instructions:
id -u
# oc-p6-install.block - ROOT shell (enter sudo -i separately first). Install OC/meter tooling + Geekbench 6. No reboot. No X restart.
# Why: operator wants official benchmarks (Geekbench 6 + Unigine Superposition) and Linux-native OC tooling (gwe, cpupower, lm_sensors, nvtop), plus power/thermal meters and CPU stability stress (stress-ng, turbostat).
# Gate: xbps transaction completes; command -v lines each print a path; /usr/local/bin/geekbench6 exists and ls -l shows the Geekbench dir.
# Rollback: xbps-remove -y gwe lm_sensors cpupower nvtop stress-ng turbostat wget then rm /usr/local/bin/geekbench6 then rm -rf /opt/geekbench then rm /root/Geekbench-6.5.0-Linux.tar.gz
# Note: gwe is GreenWithEnvy 0.15.5 from the Void repo (archived upstream, still packaged and working). Superposition is downloaded by the operator in the user block (1.5GB).
df -h /
xbps-install -S
xbps-install -y gwe lm_sensors cpupower nvtop stress-ng turbostat wget
xbps-pkgdb -a
wget -O /root/Geekbench-6.5.0-Linux.tar.gz https://cdn.geekbench.com/Geekbench-6.5.0-Linux.tar.gz
mkdir -p /opt/geekbench
tar -xzf /root/Geekbench-6.5.0-Linux.tar.gz -C /opt/geekbench
ls -l /opt/geekbench/
ln -sf /opt/geekbench/Geekbench-6.5.0-Linux/geekbench6 /usr/local/bin/geekbench6
command -v gwe
command -v sensors
command -v cpupower
command -v nvtop
command -v stress-ng
command -v turbostat
command -v geekbench6
ls -l /usr/local/bin/geekbench6
date

oc-p7-baseline.desc: official compare scores at stock = the meter bar for the undervolt + overclock. Geekbench 6 uploads to geekbench.com. Unigine Superposition posts to the global leaderboard at benchmark.unigine.com.
oc-p7-baseline.gate: paste back Geekbench CPU URL, Geekbench GPU URL, Superposition score + resolution/detail preset, the CSV tail from SECTION C, and the nvidia-smi post numbers.
oc-p7-baseline.rollback: exact inverse required before any forward re-run (MASTER qualityGate)
oc-p7-baseline.instructions:
id -u
# oc-p7-baseline.block - USER shell (sd), in X session. STOCK BASELINE benchmark protocol. Do this BEFORE any overclock.
# Why: official compare scores at stock = the meter bar for the undervolt + overclock. Geekbench 6 uploads to geekbench.com. Unigine Superposition posts to the global leaderboard at benchmark.unigine.com.
# Procedure: two terminals below. Run SECTION A in terminal 1 (it runs until Ctrl+C). Run SECTION B in terminal 2. When B is done, Ctrl+C terminal 1, then run SECTION C.
# Gate: paste back Geekbench CPU URL, Geekbench GPU URL, Superposition score + resolution/detail preset, the CSV tail from SECTION C, and the nvidia-smi post numbers.
# NOTE for operator: same preset for every run forever. Superposition default choice = 1080p Extreme; if the free build only offers 1080p Standard or 1080p High, use that and say which one.
# SECTION A - terminal 1: start the power/thermal meter on the GPU (logs every second until Ctrl+C)
mkdir -p /home/sd/oc-meters
nvidia-smi dmon -s pucvt -d 1 -o csv -f /home/sd/oc-meters/gpu-base.csv
# SECTION B - terminal 2: CPU + GPU official benchmarks at stock
geekbench6 --benchmark
geekbench6 --compute
# Superposition - download and install (about 1.5GB, official free Linux build)
wget -O /home/sd/Downloads/Unigine_Superposition-1.1.run https://assets.unigine.com/d/Unigine_Superposition-1.1.run
chmod +x /home/sd/Downloads/Unigine_Superposition-1.1.run
/home/sd/Downloads/Unigine_Superposition-1.1.run
# GUI opens: choose preset above, press Benchmark, at the end enter a name for the leaderboard and submit, then note the score.
# SECTION C - terminal 1 after Ctrl+C: stop the meter, then print the log tail and post-run numbers
tail -20 /home/sd/oc-meters/gpu-base.csv
nvidia-smi -q -d POWER,TEMPERATURE,CLOCK
sensors
date
